title: Error from replacing one polynomial input
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ be a real coefficient family on subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ whose coefficients vanish on sets of size greater than $k+1$. Fix a coordinate $i$, and let $X_j,Y_j:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be two coordinate families, each independent within itself, such that $X_j=Y_j$ as functions whenever $j\ne i$. For every coordinate, both inputs satisfy the fourth-order invariance moment conditions: their first and third moments are zero, their second moment is one, and their fourth moment is at most $9$ (with finite fourth moment and almost-everywhere measurability). If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$, $C\ge0$, and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every real $t$, then $\left|\mathbb E[\psi(F(X))]-\mathbb E[\psi(F(Y))]\right|\le \frac{C}{12}9^{k+1}\,\mathrm{Inf}_i[F]^2$, where $F(X)(\omega)=\sum_S F(S)\prod_{j\in S}X_j(\omega)$ and the influence is that of the Boolean-cube evaluation of $F$.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ and $Y$ are each independent coordinate families
Each coordinate of $X$ and $Y$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions under $\mu$
The absolute value of the fourth derivative of $\psi$ is bounded by $C$ everywhere
replaced: Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ be a real multilinear polynomial and fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Suppose $F$ has degree at most $k+1$, and $X,Y$ are real input families on one probability space, each independent within itself, agreeing as functions at every coordinate other than $i$. Every input is measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$ and $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}|$ everywhere, then $|\mathbb E\psi(F(X))-\mathbb E\psi(F(Y))|\le(C/12)9^{k+1} I_i(F)^2$, where $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$.
